title: Breast cancer proteomics and phosphoproteomics
projectDescription: Breast cancer tissue pieces from the SCAN-B project were subjected to multiomics analysis. The flow-throughs from RNA seq were here analyzed using protoemics and phosphoproteomics
sampleProcessingProtocol: Approximately 100 µg protein per sample flow-throughs from AllPrep (Qiagen) were transfered to 96-well plates and prepared for proteomics and phosphoproteomics on a KingFisher Flex robot after reduction and alkylation for one hour using TCAP-HCl and 2-CAA. Protein Aggregation Capture with MagReSyn Hydroxyl beads and digestion using LysC (1:500) and Trypsin (1:1000) overnight. TFA was added to a final concentration of 1% and peptides were dried and stored at -80 degrees C until desalting using SepPak 40 mg tC18 96-well plates (proteomics) or Oasis Prime HLB 10 mg 96-well plates (phosphoprotoemics). Approximately 600 ng peptides (based n NanoDrop) were loaded on EvoTips for protoemics. For phosphoproteomics MagReSyn Zr-IMAC HP beads were used for enrichment in the KingFisher robot and the entire eluate was loaded on Evotips before LC-MS. An Evosep One with a 15 cm in-house packed fused silica capillary with emitter tip and frit (75 µM ID, ReproSil-Pur 1.9 µm C18 material) was used for peptide sepration with 20 SPD Whisper for full proteome and 40 SPD Whisper for phosphoproteome analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: DIA raw data files were converted to mzML using msconvert of ProteoWizard with demultiplexing of staggered windows. DIA-NN version 1.8.1 was used in library-free mode for quantification of peptides with max one missed cleavage. For phosphoproteome data 2 variable Phospho(STY) modifications were allowed. The search was performed using two UniProt databases with canonical sequences in one and additional isoforms and variants in the other, downloaded June 2023, and common contaminants from https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00145.
